decisive_items: MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrated decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5
lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss
response.rationale: The vignette describes new fever, back pain, leg weakness, and MRI findings of L4-L5 signal changes with positive blood cultures, all pointing to spondylodiscitis. R3 directly matches the imaging pattern and clinical syndrome. R1 identifies the causative organism but is not the diagnosis itself. R2 and R4 are prior conditions unrelated to the acute presentation.

rejected.why: Esophageal cancer is the underlying malignancy, not the current acute spinal syndrome.
Anastomotic fistula was a prior complication, resolved by salvage reconstruction; not the cause of new back pain and MRI changes.
Enterobacter cloacae is the pathogen, but the most likely diagnosis is the spinal infection (spondylodiscitis) it causes.
